hypotheses.description: market (last clean print) and Binance fair of the filled side 5-60 s after cluster fills vs other makers' fills; by counterparty and taker order size
hypotheses.verdict: mechanism: buys ~2.9 c below Binance fair when the market trades below Binance; in BUILD the market rose 0.7 c above the pre-fill print within 60 s while Binance fell (market catching up with Binance); in VALIDATE fills were adversely selected on the next minute's spot (-1.6 c vs -0.3 c for other makers; broad, not one sniper) = the edge decay; caveat: our Binance fair is over-confident and reverts toward the fill price after fills (40% of fills are at or above it), so only the BUILD-vs-VALIDATE comparison of post-fill fair moves is clean; VALIDATE losses concentrate in near-the-money mid-window fills

hypotheses.description: cluster share of bid hits on s vs the 3-s change of the Binance fair of s
hypotheses.verdict: reprices/cancels faster than the average competing maker after Binance moves (less so in VALIDATE)

hypotheses.verdict: fixed size ladder, no edge-dependent sizing; the ladder shrank from 500/1000 to 500/250/125

previous_wall_claims.wall_reason: diminishing returns (brief): best VALIDATE presence AUC on the clean metric 0.7592 (iteration 1, clean equivalent) -> 0.7634 (iteration 2) -> 0.7634 (iteration 3), +0.004 over the last two iterations, which tried 12 and 12 new families. Structural cap: which BTC 5m windows the cluster trades is an operator schedule with no public correlate (window AUC 0.47-0.58 from tape statistics, taker mix, competitor identity, spot regime, listing fields; oracle on/off ceiling 0.862). Not an information wall on quotes: no lead over Binance 1-s data, and it reprices faster than other makers.
previous_wall_claims.outcome: not accepted under the find-the-strategy brief (2026-10-31): no audit, catalog not worked through
